name: Dogfood 039: RFC 0037 web UI ergonomic improvements

native_delegation.instruction: Use native delegation aggressively for parallelizable work that meets the criteria in the implement prompt. The parent session remains accountable for Striatum artifacts, write scope, verification, and completion. Long-running `make test` invocations should be bounded — break large test files into smaller focused verifications to avoid lease expiry beyond the documented ~30-minute window.

Use sub-agents aggressively for bounded independent research, review, and code/test/doc authorship. Do not let native delegation obscure the parent session's artifact and verdict accountability. When asked to write a review or design artifact, write the file directly in the single supervised invocation; do not ask the operator clarifying questions and exit without producing the artifact (see dogfood-037 OPERATOR_REPORT.md intervention #5 for the friction pattern this constraint addresses). If permission to call striatum ack is denied, write the artifact and exit normally; the operator publishes on your behalf.

Use local sub-agents only for bounded independent work. Do not rely on remote agent-to-agent delegation or hidden state as provenance. When asked to write an artifact, write the file directly in the single supervised invocation; do not surface strategy and ask the operator to proceed (see dogfood-036 OPERATOR_REPORT.md intervention #2 for the friction pattern). When writing finding artifacts, use the EXACT `striatum.finding.v1` front-matter shape: `verdict_intent` (not `verdict`); `severity` from {low,medium,high,critical} (not `none`); `tags` as a JSON array; the `author: ...` byline is a plain markdown line AFTER the front-matter block, NOT a key inside it. Handoff artifacts (DESIGN.md) do not need front matter; just the plain `author: <slug>` byline.

jobs.title: Design RFC 0037 web UI improvements from Codex
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0037: web UI ergonomic improvements. Cover: concrete file-by-file edits to `src/striatum/web/templates/` and `src/striatum/web/static/`; new JS files (`base.js`, `run_list.js`, `workflows_index.js`); the 10 ergonomic wins enumerated in the RFC (run-list filter + duration; workflows-index filter + last-modified; doctor grouping + terminal-hide toggle; localtime toggle; graph-node tooltips; keyboard shortcuts; app.css dark-mode parity; next-actions promotion; empty-state copy; no new runtime deps). State the JS architecture (vanilla, no framework, no bundler), the localStorage key naming convention, the data-island pattern for client-side filtering, and the test strategy (existing UI snapshot tests + new test files for the JS modules where reasonable).

jobs.title: Design RFC 0037 web UI improvements from Claude Code
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0037 emphasizing the first-time-user experience and the affordance grammar that makes each gap into a discoverable surface. Focus on: filter row UX (placeholder text, default state, persistence semantics, clear-filter affordance); duration column format (mm:ss for under 1h, hh:mm for longer); localtime toggle visual placement + state indicator; keyboard shortcut overlay UX (when to show, how to dismiss, what keys are listed); empty-state copy quality bar (specific, actionable, with copy-paste CLI examples); next-actions panel banner layout (when shown, when hidden, accessibility considerations); doctor grouping default-collapsed behavior. Be specific: each ergonomic decision should have a one-line justification.

jobs.title: Design RFC 0037 web UI improvements from Gemini
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0037 with attention to: accessibility (keyboard navigation completeness, focus management, ARIA labels for filter pills, dialog semantics for the keyboard-shortcut help overlay); responsive behavior at narrow viewports (the RFC's non-goal of mobile-first redesign still means widgets shouldn't break on a 1024px-wide laptop); state persistence layering (localStorage for filter state, default-state-on-first-visit, migration when keys change); dark-mode parity audit checklist (which app.css classes need explicit dark blocks); empty-state illustration choice (simple ASCII, system emoji, or inline SVG icon — pick one and explain). Test strategy: existing UI snapshot tests + new JS unit tests where reasonable + manual checklist for the things that can't be automated.

jobs.title: Synthesize RFC 0037 web UI improvements implementation plan
jobs.objective: Reconcile all three fresh design artifacts into one implementation plan for RFC 0037. Pick the concrete JS architecture (vanilla, no framework, no bundler), localStorage key naming convention, data-island pattern, dark-mode parity audit checklist, accessibility checklist, empty-state illustration choice. Explicitly defer: filter-state-in-querystring (V1.5); sticky-positioned next-actions banner (future RFC if requested); keyboard-shortcut configurability (future RFC); per-doctor-problem-kind doc anchors that don't exist yet in HOW_TO_HUMAN (the implementer creates the anchors as part of this work or notes them as defer-to-doc-pass). State the staging plan: localtime + base.js scaffold first (lowest risk), then run-list filters, then workflows filters, then doctor grouping, then graph tooltips, then next-actions promotion, then app.css dark-mode parity, then empty-state copy, then docs.

jobs.title: Ergonomics-DX review of RFC 0037 design
jobs.objective: Review the synthesized RFC 0037 plan under ergonomics_dx posture. Verdict acceptance means the affordances are discoverable and consistent from a first-time-user perspective. Evaluate: are the filter UX choices specific and actionable? Does the localtime toggle have a visible state indicator? Are the keyboard shortcuts mnemonic + discoverable via the `?` help overlay? Is the empty-state copy specific (with copy-paste CLI examples) or boilerplate? Is the dark-mode parity audit complete (every app.css class listed)? Is the JS architecture honest (vanilla, no framework, no bundler — or has it crept toward complexity)? Is the staging plan low-risk-first? Are the deferred items clearly named? IMPORTANT: write the REVIEW.md artifact directly in this single supervised invocation. Use the EXACT `striatum.finding.v1` front-matter shape (`verdict_intent` not `verdict`; `severity` from {low,medium,high,critical}; `tags` as JSON array; `author: ...` as plain markdown line after the front-matter block, NOT a key inside it).

jobs.title: Implement RFC 0037 web UI improvements
jobs.objective: Implement only the reviewed and accepted scope in docs/dogfood/039/DESIGN_SYNTHESIS.md. Use sub-agents AGGRESSIVELY per the implement prompt — this is a UI dogfood with many parallelizable surfaces (one sub-agent per template + per JS file + per CSS dark-mode block + per empty-state + per doc surface). Ship: localtime toggle + base.js scaffold; run-list filter + duration column + empty state; workflows-index filter + last-modified + empty state; doctor grouping + terminal-hide toggle + empty state; graph node tooltips; keyboard shortcuts + help overlay; app.css dark-mode parity; next-actions promotion on run detail; documentation updates (HOW_TO_HUMAN screenshots optional but linked; CHANGELOG entry; SPEC cross-reference if applicable). No new runtime dependencies, no SPA conversion, no visual redesign. Cycle exhaustion at max_iterations=2 → operator records a decision and continues with the latest verdict.

jobs.title: Ergonomics-DX review of RFC 0037 build
jobs.objective: Review the implementation under the ergonomics_dx posture. Actually try the surfaces if you can: walk through the run list filter, workflows index filter, doctor grouping, localtime toggle, keyboard shortcuts, graph tooltips. Verify: filter state persists in localStorage across reloads; duration column shows correct format; doctor groups + collapses correctly; localtime toggle rewrites every `<time>` element; keyboard shortcuts disabled when focus is on inputs; help overlay is dismissable; dark-mode parity is complete across app.css; next-actions banner appears for non-terminal runs only; empty-state copy is specific and actionable. Verify no new runtime deps (no new package.json, no node_modules, no bundler entry). IMPORTANT: write the REVIEW.md artifact directly. If permission to call striatum ack is denied, write the artifact and exit normally; do not ask the operator clarifying questions and exit without producing the artifact (see dogfood-037 OPERATOR_REPORT.md intervention #5).
